name_story.story: Zahid can be understood through the Arabic form زَاهِد, whose central sense is zahid; ascetic, abstinent. Zahid is Arabic زَاهِد (Zāhid), the active participle of زَهِدَ, meaning 'ascetic'.

faq.a: Zahid is associated with the Arabic form زَاهِد, whose core sense is zahid; ascetic, abstinent.

faq.q: What is the origin of Zahid?
faq.a: Zahid is associated with Arabic. Zahid is Arabic زَاهِد (Zāhid), the active participle of زَهِدَ, meaning 'ascetic'.
Yes — the underlying form زَاهِد is Arabic.
Zahid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zahid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zāhid is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zahid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zahid is rendered زاہد and carries the sense زاہد، پرہیزگار.

faq.q: What does Zahid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zahid is rendered زاهد and carries the sense زاهد، پارسا.
A romanized syllable approximation is za-hid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zahid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zahid, zahid. Script forms are زاهد, زاہد, زَاهِد, ज़ाहिद.

faq.q: Is Zahid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
